records.title: Barriers and Facilitators to Technology Use Among Caregivers of Homebound Older Adults: Descriptive Qualitative Study
records.abstract: Homebound older adults (≥60 y) and their informal family caregivers face multiple challenges in meeting their instrumental, emotional, and informational needs, which result in lower functional status, multiple comorbidities, and poorer mental health. Caregivers are tasked with providing uncompensated care for medically complex older adults, often without formal health care training. This circumstance may translate to high levels of burden and greater vulnerability to social isolation and loneliness, which may precipitate chronic stress and compromise caregiver health. In recent years, numerous health-focused technologies assisting with health-promoting behaviors such as physical activity, stress management, and nutritional tracking have emerged. However, little is known about how these tools are adopted by family caregivers of homebound older adults.  This descriptive qualitative study aimed to explore how caregivers of homebound older adults perceive technology in the context of supporting caregiving and aging in place through focus groups and one-on-one interviews.  We conducted a descriptive qualitative study using in-person and online video conference focus group methodology with 40 individuals (32 caregivers, 6 clinicians, and 2 additional key informants) to explore perspectives on caregivers’ use of technology to support their caregiving activities. Participants completed a brief sociodemographic questionnaire prior to all interviews. Procedures for thematic analysis were used to analyze the data and identify emerging themes.  Three main themes (and related subthemes) emerged from the data: (1) these technologies are not designed for people like us, (2) balancing the scales, and (3) preserving a sense of self. Caregivers’ experiences with technology are marked by a paradox: the same technologies that can ease caregiving activities may also impose new burdens through additional costs, uncertainty, learning demands, and emotional strain.  Caregivers should not navigate these technological tensions alone. Realizing the promise of technology requires more than innovative tools—it demands caregiver-centered design, accessible and equitable implementation strategies, and sustained clinical and health system support to ensure that technology alleviates, rather than amplifies, caregiver burden.

records.title: Marital Status, Living Arrangement, and Aging Well in China
records.abstract: This study explores the relationship between marital status, living arrangements, and aging well among Chinese adults aged 50 and older.  Using data from the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS), we developed a multidimensional measure of aging well (physiological, functional, cognitive, psychological, and subjective). Analysis was based on a five-category typology of marital and living arrangements.  A clear hierarchy emerged in the findings: married individuals co-residing with spouses experienced the most favorable outcomes, while unmarried individuals living alone faced the greatest challenges. Non-traditional arrangements (e.g., married living apart) also showed significant difficulties, particularly in subjective well-being. These associations were moderated by socio-demographic factors, with disparities being less pronounced among respondents aged 75+, retirees, urban residents, and those with healthier lifestyles. Discussion The findings underscore the enduring importance of co-resident marital relationships while highlighting the evolving influence of diverse family arrangements on the well-being of older adults in China.

records.abstract: Hot weather is an established cardiovascular hazard, but patient-level evidence on how clinical vulnerability, cooling constraints and barriers to care interact in older cardiology outpatients remains limited.  We conducted a convergent mixed- study in the cardiology outpatient clinic of a tertiary university hospital in Zonguldak, Türkiye, from June to August 2026. A total of 680 consecutively recruited patients aged ≥ 65 years completed a structured interviewer-administered survey covering heat-related symptoms, housing and cooling capacity, health-care access and frailty assessed using the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS). The primary outcome was self-reported heat-related worsening of cardiovascular symptoms; secondary outcomes included care delay and marked impact on daily life. Multivariable logistic regression was used, and a pragmatic seven-domain heat-vulnerability index was explored. Twenty purposively sampled participants underwent semi-structured interviews, analysed thematically and integrated with the quantitative findings.  Mean age was 71.3 ± 5.3 years and 48.1% were women. Inadequate effective cooling was reported by 82.4%, at least two heat-related symptoms by 75.9%, and heat-related care delay by 30.9%. Among participants giving a definite response, 52.1% reported symptom worsening, independently associated with heart failure (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.86, 95% CI 1.18–2.95), prolonged hot indoor exposure (aOR 1.82, 1.19–2.81), summer transport difficulty (aOR 1.65, 1.08–2.53) and greater frailty (aOR per CFS point 1.30, 1.09–1.55). Care delay was associated with limited or absent daytime support (aOR 2.99, 2.05–4.35), transport difficulty (aOR 2.59, 1.67–4.00), living alone (aOR 2.45, 1.62–3.70) and insufficient income (aOR 2.02, 1.34–3.03). Symptom worsening, care delay and daily-life impact increased across vulnerability categories. Interviews showed that effective cooling, access to care and social support depended on their practical usability rather than nominal availability.  Heat-related burden in older cardiology outpatients extends beyond acute events to symptoms, daily functioning and continuity of care, consistent with a multidimensional pattern of clinical, environmental and social vulnerability. Frailty, effective cooling, transport and reliable support may be relevant domains for brief heat-health discussions in outpatient cardiovascular care. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

records.title: Changes in Patterns of Health Care Use Among Older Adults in Singapore Across a Decade: Repeated Nationwide Cross-Sectional Survey
records.abstract: There is limited evidence on the patterns of health care use among older adults in Singapore over the past decade.  This study examines whether the proportion of specific services used within sociodemographic subgroups, the factors associated with health care use, and the network structure of health care use have changed over a decade.  We used data from 2 repeated nationwide cross-sectional surveys of Singapore residents aged 60 years and older, conducted in 2013 (n=2565) and 2023 (n=2010). Health care service use was obtained from an adapted version of the Client Service Receipt Inventory and analyzed using multivariable logistic regression and network analysis.  The most significant changes between 2013 and 2023 were in the proportions of older adults who had consulted private hospital/clinic doctors (decreased by 4.6 percentage points; n=655, 26.5% vs n=425, 21.9%; P =.02), consulted public and private dentists (increased by 6.4 percentage points; n=215, 11.6% vs n=269, 18%; P P  This study provides important data on population-level changes in health care usage among older adults across the decade from 2013 to 2023, which will help policymakers ensure better health care delivery for older adults.

records.title: Shifting paradigms: key tensions in putting the person’s narrative central in improving quality of care in Dutch nursing homes
records.abstract: and  Narrative approaches to quality improvement are increasingly adopted by long-term care organizations to gain insight into quality from the perspectives of older persons. However, it remains unclear how organizations experience the organizational challenges of embedding these approaches in new quality improvement routines and policies. This study aims to investigate what tensions arise when organizing and embedding narrative approaches and how organizations respond to these tensions. Research Design and  An exploratory qualitative multiple-method design consisting of observations, semi-structured interviews and document analysis was used. Data were collected in Dutch nursing homes between February 2024 and June 2025. To gain in-depth and broader insights, organizations were observed for a longer period (n = 2) and interviews were conducted with other organizations (n = 9) about organizing a narrative approach.  : Four tensions were identified: 1) steering on pre-determined themes vs. emergent themes from experiences 2) abstracting narratives into broad quality terms vs. preserving the richness of narratives; 3) organizing quality top-down and in silos vs. as a collaborative and dynamic process; and 4) accounting for compliance vs. learning for improvement.  The tensions show that organizing a narrative process goes beyond organizational challenges, but requires a paradigm shift in how organizations view and organize quality improvement. It requires a different way of data collection, analysis and collaboration and emphasizes relationality and learning over individualized accounting. When organizations get stuck between two different quality paradigms, this can lead to several risks. The implications, risks and potential of narrative approaches are discussed.

records.title: Process evaluation of a complex intervention to improve the oral health of nursing home residents (MundZaRR): a multimethod study
records.abstract: The oral health of nursing home residents is often poor. In the cluster-randomised controlled MundZaRR trial, a complex intervention to improve oral health was investigated across 18 nursing homes ( n = 271 participants). A comprehensive process evaluation aimed to explore the experiences of various target groups and gain insights into the implementation of the intervention.  The process evaluation followed international guidelines. The study was conducted in Germany and the data collection took place between July 2022 and October 2023 and comprised 23 individual, semi-structured interviews and three focus groups with dentists, dental assistants, nursing home managers and staff, and members of the resident council, 20 participatory observations, written surveys, structured protocols and document analysis. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively; qualitative data were analysed using content analysis.  Three educational training courses over approximately nine hours for dentists and dental assistants were performed largely as planned and evaluated positively. The intervention could not be implemented in one out of nine nursing homes due to staff and time shortages, and the remaining intervention clusters showed considerable variations in implementation fidelity and cooperation between dental assistants and nursing home staff. Participatory observations revealed that individual oral care recommendations were only completely implemented in around half of the observed participants and that more specific oral care measures (e.g., interdental cleaning) were only rarely performed. The main barriers to the intervention’s implementation were staff and time shortages, lack of interest or engagement of nursing staff, and individual resident barriers (e.g., poor health condition, uncooperative behaviour). The COVID-19 pandemic posed a major challenge during the recruitment phase, but predominantly did not affect the further course of the study, according to the participating target groups.  Despite the overall positive perception of the intervention concept by the target groups, we found several inconsistencies in the implementation across the nursing homes of the intervention group. The barriers identified can provide indications for the future development and implementation of comparable oral health interventions in the nursing home setting. records.title: Health literacy in action through community-based participatory research: the ENABLE programme for indigenous older adults in Taiwan
records.abstract: Nutritional status and functional capacity are closely linked and contribute to healthy longevity. Given geographic isolation, Indigenous older adults are more likely to experience limited food diversity and suboptimal diets, increasing cardiometabolic risk in later life. Indigenous Taiwanese communities have distinct cultural identities, lifestyles, and food systems; therefore, health promotion programmes combining professional advice with culturally appropriate approaches are crucial.  This community-based participatory research (CBPR), titled ‘Engaging Native Abilities to Boost Lifestyle Enhancement’ (ENABLE), co-created nutrition and cooking workshops with the Indigenous Tsou community in Taiwan. Photovoice-facilitated focus groups were conducted with nine Indigenous older adults to explore dietary patterns before and after the workshops. Post-workshop interviews were conducted with 16 participants, including nine older adults and seven co-organisers.  The findings reveal that health literacy is constructed and embodied in everyday practices through three interrelated processes shaped by health needs, social roles, and relational responsibility. First, ‘negotiating dietary decisions with health needs’ involves dialogue between traditional and scientific knowledge about food choice transitions. For example, some participants described transitioning from traditional roasted pork to fish in response to changes in chewing ability. Second, ‘engaging place-based adaptive strategies within lifestyles’ supports food access and maintenance of social roles. For example, work is central to Indigenous life, shaping identity, autonomy, and a sense of achievement; participants incorporated dietary portion control into their lifestyles to manage weight while maintaining strength for work. Third, ‘mobilising individual agency for collective well-being’ extends nutritional awareness to family and community members.  The CBPR approach, grounded in the lived experiences of Indigenous older adults, can shape a tailored dietary intervention. Meaningful engagement in Indigenous health research is strengthened by mutual understanding, shared action, and reflexive dialogue. Health literacy may support the agency of Indigenous older adults and local health sectors; however, its sustained effects in addressing structural barriers and supporting healthy ageing in place warrant further examination. Given the centrality of work in Indigenous life, health promotion activities may benefit from remaining flexible and collaborating with occupational groups to better connect working-aged adults, those transitioning into retirement, and older adults with increasing health needs.

records.title: Greater psychosocial well-being predicts higher physical activity in older adults with musculoskeletal pain: evidence from observational and simulation models
records.abstract: Musculoskeletal pain and psychosocial well-being both influence leisure-time physical activity (LTPA) in older adults, but their combined impact remains poorly understood. This study examines the impact of musculoskeletal pain and psychosocial well-being on LTPA trajectories in older adults and estimates the potential impact of improved energy levels on LTPA using simulation modeling.  In a community-based cohort of 2,209 older adults, we investigated whether baseline musculoskeletal and psychosocial well-being (perceived energy and social engagement) predicted 9-year LTPA trajectories. Two LTPA trajectory groups were identified: lower (45%, median[range]: 11[0–86] minutes walking/week) and higher (55%, median[range]: 111[10–1610] minutes walking/week). Logistic regression models examined associations of musculoskeletal pain, energy, and social engagement with LTPA trajectory group adjusting for demographics, health behaviors, and comorbidities. An interaction of psychosocial well-being by musculoskeletal pain was tested. A simulation analysis estimated how increasing energy among older adults with musculoskeletal pain could influence predicted LTPA group membership, and the number needed to treat (NNT) was calculated.  Baseline perceived energy, but not social engagement or musculoskeletal pain, consistently ranked among the top three predictors of LTPA across models. In adjusted logistic regression models, musculoskeletal pain was associated with a 40% lower likelihood of being in the higher LTPA trajectory; high energy corresponded with a 73% higher likelihood of being in the higher LTPA trajectory. Social engagement was associated with 33% higher LTPA, but only among men. The interaction between musculoskeletal pain and energy was not significant. After reassigning higher energy levels to older adults with low energy and musculoskeletal pain, the predicted probability of being in the higher LTPA trajectory increased from 41% to 50%, yielding an NNT of 11.  Perceived energy is a strong, independent predictor of LTPA, even in the presence of musculoskeletal pain. Simulated increase in energy among 11 older adults with pain corresponded with one additional person in the higher LTPA trajectory, an effect comparable to current behavioral interventions. Supporting psychosocial wellbeing may offer a valuable approach to promoting LTPA in older adults alongside pain management.

records.title: Effects of professional trainer-led and trained volunteer-led bodyweight training programs on physical fitness and body composition of rural community-dwelling older adults
records.abstract: and  Physical inactivity accelerates functional decline in rural older adults with limited exercise resources. Although bodyweight training is scalable, whether benefits depend on professional supervision remains unclear. We compared professional- and trained volunteer-led bodyweight training programs (BWTP) on functional fitness and body composition in rural community-dwelling older adults. Research Design and  In this quasi-experimental, community-based, three-group pretest-posttest study with community-level allocation (April 2021-January 2022), adults aged ≥65 years who were independent in activities of daily living and not engaged in other regular exercise programs were assigned to a professional trainer, trained volunteer, or comparison group. The intervention groups received a 12-week BWTP. Functional fitness and body composition were assessed pre- and postintervention, and Group × Time effects were examined using two-way mixed ANOVA.  Among 72 participants (Professional Trainer Group, PTG, n = 25; Volunteer Trainer Group, VTG, n = 22; Comparison Group, CG, n = 25), several functional fitness outcomes showed significant Group × Time interactions (p ≤ .003; partial η² = .155-.248). Both intervention groups improved mobility and postural stability more than the CG. PTG improved handgrip strength versus CG (Hedges’ g = 0.85), whereas VTG showed the largest lower-limb muscular endurance gain (g = 1.26). CG declined in several functional measures. No body-composition outcome remained significant after adjustment.  Trained volunteer-led BWTP may extend exercise delivery and support functional fitness in resource-limited rural communities. Hybrid models with professional oversight warrant evaluation because body-composition effects did not persist after multiplicity adjustment.

records.title: What Determines the Preference to Coreside? Applying the Andersen-Newman Framework to a Lagged Longitudinal Analysis Among Older Adults in China
records.abstract: Using longitudinal data, we investigate changes in coresidence preference of Chinese older adults and, with application of the Andersen-Newman framework, examine factors contributing to coresidence preference.  Data come from five waves of the Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey collected between 2005 and 2018. A random-effect model uses baseline covariates to predict coresidence preference at follow-up between two adjacent waves, controlling for baseline preference and changes in actual living arrangement between baseline and follow-up.  Regressions showed enabling factors played a more robust role in shaping coresidence preference than time-invariant personal characteristics. Interactions found that some personal characteristics reinforced the effect of enabling factors. Discussion Coresidence is not necessarily the most sought-after living arrangement among older Chinese. What is regarded as “traditional” may instead reflect circumstantial factors, such that a coresidential living arrangement is best suited to an older person’s particular situation.

records.title: Identification of Novel Protein Biomarkers and Lifestyle-Modifiable Targets for Osteoporosis: Evidence from Mendelian Randomization and Colocalization Analyses
records.journal: The Journals of Gerontology, Series A: Biological Sciences and Medical Sciences
records.abstract: Osteoporosis (OP), a degenerative bone disease prevalent in aging populations, can lead to various complications and significantly impair the quality of life of elderly patients. We aimed to identify OP-related protein biomarkers and modifiable lifestyle factors for OP prevention in older adults.  Summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) and colocalization analyses were conducted to assess the possible causal effects of plasma protein on OP. Genetic data for plasma proteins were derived from the deCODE (4907 proteins) and UK Biobank-PPP (2923 proteins) datasets. OP summary statistics were obtained from the FinnGen study (10,461 cases). Two-sample Mendelian randomization (TSMR) analyses were subsequently performed to evaluate the effects of lifestyle factors on OP-related proteins.  Primary SMR analysis identified 31 and 24 OP-related proteins in the deCODE and UKB-PPP cohorts, respectively. Cross-analysis of both datasets identified nine OP-related plasma protein targets. Among them, RSPO3 showed moderate evidence of colocalization with OP (PP.H4 = 0.643). TSMR analysis suggested that genetically predicted higher body mass index (BMI) was associated with increased RSPO3 levels (β = 0.08, 95% CI 0.02 to 0.14, p = 0.001), whereas type 2 diabetes (T2DM) was associated with lower RSPO3 levels (β = -5.71, 95% CI -11.16 to -0.26, p = 0.045).  This study identified nine plasma protein biomarkers with genetic evidence supporting their association with OP risk, with RSPO3 showing the strongest supportive evidence among the prioritized targets. These findings offer new insights into OP etiology and highlight how metabolic traits may influence bone health via specific protein mediators.

records.title: Anterior subcutaneous pelvic internal fixation versus conservative treatment for type iib and iic fragility fractures of the pelvis in older adults: a multicentre retrospective study
records.abstract: To compare anterior subcutaneous pelvic internal fixation with conservative treatment in older adults with type IIb and IIc fragility fractures of the pelvis (FFP).  We included 217 patients with type IIb or IIc FFP treated at five trauma centres between January 2020 and December 2022 (operative, n = 86; conservative, n = 131). Demographics, comorbidities, length of stay, complications, costs, visual analogue scale (VAS) pain scores, mortality, Barthel Index (BI), instrumental activities of daily living (IADL) score and walking ability were analysed. Follow-up was ≥ 1 year. Multivariable regression and Kaplan–Meier analyses were performed.  Follow-up duration did not differ between groups (28.3 ± 13.2 vs. 29.0 ± 17.7 months; P = 0.733). The conservative group was older, with more comorbidities and complications but shorter stays and lower costs. Full weight-bearing occurred earlier in the operative group, whereas fracture-healing time did not differ. After adjustment, surgery was associated with lower odds of poorer walking ability (OR = 0.081, P = 0.001), higher BI (B = 3.318, P = 0.018) and lower VAS pain scores (B = − 1.219, P P = 0.109). Mortality did not differ significantly (log-rank P = 0.074).  Patients who underwent surgery were younger, had better pre-injury function and showed more favourable outcomes. Causality remains uncertain because of the retrospective design, baseline imbalances and strong correlation between pre- and post-injury walking ability. Surgical indications should balance potential benefits against higher costs and procedure-related complications.

records.title: Development and Evaluation of WELSH: An Institution-Linked Mobile Application for Older Adults in Senior Welfare Centers During COVID-19
records.abstract: COVID-19 closures of South Korean senior welfare centers isolated older adults. We developed and evaluated “WELSH,” an age-friendly, institution-linked mobile app, using the ADDIE (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation) framework.  Following needs assessments, WELSH was implemented across five Seoul centers. During a 2-week pilot, 376 older adults completed pre- and post-intervention questionnaires evaluating usability, digital literacy, and psychosocial indicators (social support, loneliness, depression).  Participants positively rated WELSH’s usability (M = 2.95/4), particularly for accessing center-linked information. Digital literacy scores significantly increased ( p  WELSH successfully maintained institutional connectivity and enhanced short-term digital competence. Practical Implications: This ADDIE-guided process provides a replicable framework for community centers to design age-friendly digital services, ensuring care continuity during crises.

records.title: Joint associations of handgrip strength and chair-stand performance with motoric cognitive risk syndrome in older adults
records.journal: The Journals of Gerontology, Series A: Biological Sciences and Medical Sciences
records.abstract: Motor dysfunction is associated with cognitive vulnerability, but whether impairments across body regions jointly contribute to motoric cognitive risk syndrome (MCR) remains unclear. We examined the independent and joint associations of handgrip strength and chair-stand test (CST) with MCR.  This cross-sectional study included 6258 dementia-free older adults (mean age 71.5 ± 6.6 years; 63.1% women) from a community-based cohort. Handgrip strength and CST performance were used to define upper- and lower-extremity motor impairment. Participants were classified as normal, handgrip weakness only, CST impairment only, or combined motor impairment. Multivariable logistic regression was performed with adjustment for demographic, socioeconomic, lifestyle, and clinical factors. Additive and multiplicative interactions were assessed.  MCR was present in 10.4% of participants. Using the A/B CST cutoff as the primary definition, adjusted odds ratios (95% confidence intervals) for MCR, compared with normal function, were 1.84 (1.14–2.97) for handgrip weakness only, 4.17 (2.97–5.85) for CST impairment only, and 9.17 (6.56–12.81) for combined motor impairment. Associations were directionally consistent across alternative CST cutoffs. A positive additive interaction was observed at the A/B CST cutoff (relative excess risk due to interaction = 3.48; attributable proportion = 0.40; and synergy index = 1.83), whereas multiplicative interaction was not positive.  Combined handgrip weakness and poorer CST performance were strongly associated with prevalent MCR. A positive additive interaction at the primary CST cutoff suggests that joint motor impairment may help characterize MCR-related vulnerability in older adults.

records.title: Treatment outcomes and influencing factors of older patients with pulmonary tuberculosis complicated with diabetes mellitus in China, 2018–2024
records.abstract: The comorbidity of pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) and diabetes mellitus (DM) is rising among adults aged ≥ 65 years in China. DM comorbidity significantly worsens PTB treatment outcomes. Population-based evidence specific to older Chinese PTB-DM patients remains scarce. This retrospective cohort study aimed to identify independent risk factors for adverse treatment outcomes in older Chinese PTB-DM patients.  Data were from the National Tuberculosis Information Management System (2018–2024). Kaplan–Meier analysis was performed to estimate overall event-free survival. Fine–Gray competing risks regression models were used to identify independent factors associated with each adverse outcome subtype, accounting for competing events.  Among 56,682 eligible patients, the median follow-up duration was 6.965 months, and the rate of adverse anti-tuberculosis treatment outcomes was 11.08%. Irregular treatment adherence ( aHR = 12.783, 95%CI : 12.008–13.607), male sex ( aHR = 1.246, 95%CI : 1.176–1.319), increased age ( aHR = 1.345–2.459), retreatment ( aHR = 1.112, 95%CI : 1.031–1.199), positive etiological test  ( aHR = 1.338, 95%CI : 1.259–1.421), comorbidities other than diabetes ( aHR = 1.234, 95%CI : 1.154–1.320), and non-guideline-concordant regimens, ( aHR = 1.096, 95%CI : 1.025–1.171) were independent risk factors for adverse treatment outcomes.  Adverse treatment outcomes in older adults with PTB-DM are driven by a range of demographic, clinical and adherence-related factors, with irregular medication adherence being the most robust predictor. These risk factors differ across adverse outcome subtypes.

records.title: Spousal Discrepancy in Perceived Importance of Care Needs Among Couples Managing Early-Stage Alzheimer’s Disease

PLWD self-reported the importance of their physical, psychological, and social needs, while caregivers provided proxy ratings. PLWD perceived addressing their physical needs as more important than did their caregivers, whereas both partners agreed on the importance of psychological and social needs. Caregivers’ greater empathic concern was associated with smaller discrepancies in the perceived importance of physical needs; greater personal distress was associated with smaller discrepancies in social needs. Caregivers’ dementia knowledge was positively associated with discrepancies in psychological needs only when relationship quality was lower. These findings highlight the importance of caregivers’ emotional responsiveness and relational dynamics in caregiver interventions, expanding the focus beyond dementia knowledge.

records.title: Sexuality and Glycosylated Hemoglobin Levels in Partnered Older Adults With Diabetes
records.abstract: We examined associations between sexual activity, sexual quality, and glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels among partnered older adults with diabetes. Using longitudinal data from the National Social Life, Health, and Aging Project, we studied 620 partnered respondents with diabetes aged 57 to 85 at baseline. We estimated mixed-effects models of sexual activity, frequency, and quality on HbA1c trajectories over ten years, including tests for gender differences.  indicated that being sexually active and having sex a few times a month were associated with more favorable HbA1c trajectories compared to being sexually inactive. records.title: Attitudes of people living with dementia and their carers towards the use of generative artificial intelligence to inform structured medication reviews
records.abstract: Polypharmacy is common in people living with dementia (PLwD) and associated with adverse outcomes. Although Structured Medication Reviews (SMRs) are recommended to optimise medication regimens, their delivery is often constrained by limited resources. Artificial intelligence (AI) may support SMRs, yet little is known about how it is perceived by PLwD and their carers. This study explored their experiences of polypharmacy, views on SMRs and attitudes towards use of AI tools in SMRs.  Semi-structured interviews with 12 PLwD experiencing polypharmacy and two focus groups with 14 carers were conducted via Microsoft Teams or telephone and analysed using Reflexive Thematic Analysis.  Two themes were constructed: participants’ perspectives on meaningful SMRs, and embracing AI while preserving patient safety and the human touch. Participants described challenges in managing polypharmacy, with carers playing a central role in supporting adherence and monitoring side effects. Experiences of SMRs varied. SMRs were most valued when clinicians were empathetic and able to offer personalised guidance. Participants viewed AI use in SMRs positively, provided that such tools were well validated and used to assist rather than replace healthcare professionals. AI was also seen as potentially reducing administrative burden and supporting more person-centred care. However, some had concerns regarding patient safety and data security, highlighting the need for appropriate regulation and human oversight.  Participants were supportive of AI use in SMRs, despite concerns about safety, data security and disclosure of AI use, and emphasised the importance of patient-clinician interactions and lived experience involvement in AI tool development.

records.title: The trajectories of comprehensive capacity of bedridden older people based on latent growth mixture models: a longitudinal study
records.abstract: Bedridden older people generally have poor comprehensive capacity and are prone to multi-system complications including pressure injuries and lower limb venous thrombosis, imposing heavy caregiving and financial burdens and severely affecting their health.  To identify distinct trajectories of ability in bedridden older people and characteristics distinguishing the trajectories, while assessing the prognostic value of these trajectories for early risk identification of pressure injury and deep-vein thrombosis (DVT). Participants Two hundred twenty six bedridden older people aged 65 years and above from two nursing homes in China.  Patients were required 5 assessments during 1-year follow-up period. Latent Growth Mixture Modelling identified distinct trajectories, multinomial logistic regression identified characteristics distinguishing the trajectories and generalised estimating equations evaluated associations between trajectories and pressure injury and DVT.  There are three distinct trajectories of comprehensive capacity among bedridden older people, including severe impairment with stable type (63.5%); moderate impairment with slowly deteriorating type (16.3%); moderate-to-severe impairment with fluctuating type (20.2%). Characteristics distinguishing the trajectories were tooth loss, hypertension, indwelling gastric tube and dysphagia. Compared with the severe impairment stable type, the other two groups had higher pressure injury risk; the moderate impairment with slowly deteriorating type also had higher DVT risk.  Capacity trajectories of bedridden older people are heterogeneous. Nurses may want to focus on those with tooth loss, hypertension, indwelling gastric tube and dysphagia to deliver targeted care. These trajectories are significantly associated with pressure injury and deep vein thrombosis risks. Their identification enables earlier risk stratification and more targeted prevention.

records.title: New horizons in adaptive capacity and heat-related health in older people: integrating frailty, energy insecurity and social resources
records.abstract: Extreme heat is a major environmental threat to healthy ageing, with older people experiencing the highest rates of heat-related morbidity and mortality. Although age-related physiological changes, multimorbidity and frailty remain key determinants of heat susceptibility, climate change, social inequalities and energy insecurity are reshaping the conditions in which older people experience and respond to thermal stress. This narrative New Horizons review integrates evidence identified through a structured, non-systematic search of peer-reviewed literature and relevant institutional reports across geriatric medicine, environmental health and climate science. It examines how frailty, intrinsic capacity, housing, energy affordability and social frailty influence the ability of older people to recognise risk, access protection and respond effectively to extreme heat. Particular attention is given to energy insecurity and summer cooling poverty, through which limited access to affordable household energy may undermine resilience. Ageing models primarily characterise individual vulnerability and functioning within the environment, whereas climate vulnerability models organise risk around exposure, sensitivity and adaptation; we use adaptive capacity to connect these perspectives by asking whether personal and contextual resources can be mobilised for protection. It may provide a conceptual basis for developing and subsequently validating a heat-adapted comprehensive geriatric assessment and for informing targeted prevention and climate adaptation policies for ageing populations.

records.title: Profiling perceived knowledge, relevance and interest across geriatric topics of health and social care professionals: multinational electronic cross-sectional survey
records.abstract: Interprofessional training is essential for high-quality care of older adults. Despite widespread recognition of its importance, evidence on perceived geriatric competence remains limited to studies on single countries or professions.  Secondary analysis of a COST Action multinational multilingual web-based survey (PROmoting GeRiAtric Medicine in countries where it is still eMergING, PROGRAMMING) conducted across the 27 European Union Member States (EU-27) and non-EU-27 countries between 9 October 2023 and 5 June 2024. Four thousand seven hundred eighty-eight professionals from 10 core health and social care groups were included. We explored perceived Knowledge, Relevance and Interest across seven domains required for comprehensive geriatric assessment: frailty, falls and mobility, delirium, depression, mild cognitive impairment and dementia screening, nutritional assessment and malnutrition, polypharmacy and deprescribing. Student’s t test; one-way analysis of variance, hierarchical clustering and latent class analysis were used to identify interprofessional differences and shared patterns across professions.  Mean age was 42.4 years (SD 11.9); 3432 (71.7%) were women; 2893 (60.4%) worked in EU-27 countries. Interprofessional differences were observed across all topics. Physiotherapists led in falls and mobility (mean 4.21, SD 0.75), pharmacists in polypharmacy and deprescribing (mean 3.51, SD 1.07), and psychologists/psychotherapists in depression (mean 3.96, SD 0.82). A medical doctors–nurses–pharmacists cluster emerged for Knowledge and Interest; 34.4% pharmacists fell in the low relevance class. Social workers and speech and language therapists showed a low Knowledge–high Interest mismatch. records.title: Social Engagement and Cognitive Function Among Chinese Older Adults During the COVID-19 Outbreak: Gender and Urban–Rural Disparities
records.abstract: This study examines the association between reduced social engagement and cognitive function among older adults in China during the COVID-19 pandemic with a focus on gender and urban–rural differences.  Using China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study data, we used OLS regression to assess changes in cognitive function before and during the pandemic and their associations with changes in physical and cognitively stimulating activities.  Cognitive function declined across social groups, with the largest decline among urban women. Moderate physical activity was not associated with less cognitive function, whereas decreased engagement in cognitively stimulating activities was associated with greater decline.  Forms of social engagement were associated with cognitive function of older adults in distinct ways, underscoring the need for a nuanced rather than uniform interpretation. The observed differences in cognitive function by subgroups suggest a need for targeted interventions to support older populations in the post-pandemic context.

records.title: Exploring Quality of Life Through Residents’ Voice in Nursing Homes: A Qualitative Study of a Montessori-Based Person-Centered Model of Care
records.abstract: Person-centered care (PCC) is the gold standard for improving the quality of life (QoL) of people living with dementia. The Montessori method represents a practical model for implementing PCC in Nursing Homes (NHs). To date, no study has documented how residents describe their QoL in NHs implementing this method using a self-report approach consistent with PCC principles. This study explores residents’ perceptions of their QoL, as well as how they relate it to the care model, using a qualitative self-assessment tool. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with twenty-nine residents from two NHs with high levels of Montessori implementation assessed using a validated tool. All interviews were analyzed using thematic analysis. Three interconnected themes emerged. The first examines the components of QoL that matter most to residents. The second explores how the care model influences these determinants. Finally, the third describes residents’ self-assessment of QoL shaped by individual factors. Our study contributes to a better understanding of the Montessori method as a comprehensive PCC model from residents’ perspectives and deepens knowledge of the extent to which it can shape their QoL. These findings also provide practical and methodological insights for evaluating QoL and guiding care models promoting QoL.

records.title: Senescence Biomarkers Predict Physical Function and Clinical Outcomes After Heart Failure Hospitalization: Insights From REHAB-HF
records.journal: The Journals of Gerontology, Series A: Biological Sciences and Medical Sciences
records.abstract: Acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) is the most common cause of hospitalization in older adults. Cellular senescence, a hallmark of aging biology, has been implicated in heart failure pathophysiology and functional decline via the pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). We evaluated the association between SASP and physical function in older adults hospitalized for ADHF.  REHAB-HF was a trial of older adults hospitalized for ADHF randomized to a novel physical rehabilitation intervention or attention control. We measured a panel of 18-SASP analytes at in-hospital baseline and at 3-month follow-up. Outcomes included short physical performance battery (SPPB) and 6-minute walk distance (6MWD). Statistical analysis included principal component analysis (PCA) of log- and z-transformed SASP values. Associations were evaluated with multivariable regression models adjusted for age, sex, and intervention arm.  Samples were available for 226 (65%) of the REHAB-HF participants with mean age (SD) 72.3 (8), 53% female, 52% HFpEF, and 53% assigned to rehab intervention. Principal Component 1 (PC1) reflected a coordinated signal across biomarkers of inflammation and immune signaling. PC1 was associated with poorer function at baseline [(SPPB -0.46 [-0.77, -0.14]; p = 0.004 and 6MWD -19.7 meters [-32.7, -6.7]; p = 0.003)]. Increasing SASP over time was associated with clinically significant reduced physical function improvement (ΔSPPB -1.80 [-2.58, -1.03]; p  Higher SASP levels were associated with poorer physical function recovery in older patients hospitalized for ADHF. These findings suggest that inflammatory SASP biomarkers may improve risk stratification and potentially guide therapeutic strategies. REHAB-HF trial is registered at clinicaltrials.gov Clinical Trial Registry NCT02196038

records.title: Intervention-Type-Specific Effects on Healthy Aging of Older Adults with Cognitive Impairment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
records.abstract: and  Healthy aging among older adults with cognitive impairment requires preserving physical, cognitive, and psychosocial functioning to sustain their independence and quality of life. However, existing interventions vary in design, delivery format, and composition, and evidence regarding their effectiveness across these three core domains remains inconsistent. This study aimed to identify the most effective intervention types for specific domains of healthy aging. Research Design and  Five electronic databases were searched for studies published from October 2015 to June 2026. Randomized controlled trials reporting at least two outcomes—among physical capability, cognitive function, or psychosocial well-being—were reviewed. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias 2 tool. A dependency-aware multilevel random-effects meta-analysis with trial-clustered robust inference was conducted in R, supplemented by moderator tests, prediction intervals, sensitivity analyses, reporting-bias assessments, and GRADE evaluations.  Multicomponent interventions were associated with beneficial effects on cognitive and psychosocial outcomes, whereas group-based interventions showed beneficial effects across all three domains and a significantly greater effect on cognitive function than individually delivered interventions. Despite substantial heterogeneity and wide prediction intervals, these findings were generally robust across sensitivity analyses.  The observed advantages of group-based delivery, particularly for cognitive function, and multicomponent approaches for cognitive and psychosocial outcomes highlight the domain-specific nature of intervention effects. These findings support tailoring intervention delivery and component configuration to the targeted domain rather than applying a uniform approach to healthy aging among older adults with cognitive impairment.

records.title: Perceptions, Knowledge, and Adaptive actions in Response to Climate Events: A Scoping Review of Climate Health Literacy among Community Dwelling Older Adults
records.abstract: and  Extreme climate events can threaten older adults’ health. The purpose of this study was to summarize existing literature on older adults’ climate health literacy, defined as their ability to find and access, understand, and act upon information related to climate-related health threats. Research Design and  A scoping review was conducted in the bibliographic databases Embase, Medline and Scopus and grey literature sources Cornell Initiative for Research on Climate and Aging and Climate Change and Human Health Literature portals with searches updated January 2026. English language studies of community-dwelling adults aged 60 years and older were included if they reported at least one aspect of climate health literacy. Quantitative data were reported as median percentages, and qualitative themes were categorized.  Fifty-nine studies, including 22,992 records for 20,296 unique participants, were included. Most recognized the health risks of extreme climate events but did not identify personal vulnerability. Television was the most cited source of information and hydration, clothing and environment modification, and activity adjustment were the most utilized adaptive actions. Barriers to adaptive actions included financial constraints, limited mobility and lack of supports. The effectiveness of studied interventions was mixed, influenced by intervention type and study design.  Despite access to information and awareness of climate-related health threats, gaps remain in personal risk perception and translation of knowledge into actions. Improving climate health literacy among older adults requires public health messaging, engagement of trustworthy authorities, and interventions addressing social and structural barriers.

records.title: Adaptive driving, not unsafe: Older drivers’ compensatory strategies and lower simulated crash risk
records.journal: The Journals of Gerontology, Series B: Psychological Sciences and Social Sciences
records.abstract: The global aging population has led to an increasing number of older active drivers. While age-related physical and cognitive changes are associated with increased crash risk, specific on-road adaptations and safety outcomes of older drivers remain unclear. This study examined distinct driving characteristics, personality traits, and cognitive processes related to decision-making among middle-aged and older drivers in a simulated driving environment.  We assessed driving performance in a high-fidelity motorcycle simulator across drivers in three age groups: middle-aged (30-54; n = 40), aged 65–74 (n = 34), and aged 75 + (75-86; n = 29). Comparative analysis focused on speed regulation, braking behavior, control stability, and accident rates. Additionally, questionnaire measures and a computerized decision-making task were employed to assess risk perception and risky decision-making.  Compared to the middle-aged group, both older groups demonstrated a significantly more conservative driving profile: lower mean speeds, fewer speeding violations, longer braking maneuvers, reduced variation in throttle control, and a lower incidence of simulated accidents. Drivers aged 75+ also reported higher perceived risk in driving scenarios and displayed diminished discrimination between risk and non-risk situations in a braking decision task. Mediation analyses showed that steering variance in the simulator and self-reported health/safety risk-taking significantly mediated the relationship between age group and number of accidents. Discussion The findings indicate that older drivers adopt proactive compensatory strategies that could result in fewer simulated accidents. These findings challenge a purely deficit-oriented perspective on older driver safety, underscoring the critical role of behavioral adaptation and strategic self-regulation in maintaining safe mobility.

records.title: Telemonitoring Adoption Among Older Adults: Sequential Mixed Methods Study of Message Framing and Structural Influence
records.abstract: Telemonitoring offers solutions for remote health management among older adults; yet, acceptance varies based on individual perceptions and presentation strategies.  This 2-phased sequential mixed  study examines the role of message framing on telemonitoring adoption among low-income older adults.  Phase 1 involved in-depth interviews with 17 older adults, identifying key facilitators (accessibility, affordability, and health benefits) and barriers (preference for in-person consultations, technological limitations, and information processing difficulties) of telemonitoring. Building on these insights, phase 2 used an experimental study with 120 participants assessing message framing effects (episodic vs thematic) and modalities (video vs photo-text) on telemonitoring adoption.  Episodic framing did not produce a significant main effect on attitudes toward telemonitoring; however, its effect was moderated by external locus of control (LOC), with episodic framing associated with more positive attitudes among participants lower in external LOC, and thematic framing more favorable among those higher in external LOC.  Convenience, cost, and health benefits emerged as key adoption drivers, while traditional consultation preferences and cognitive processing challenges posed barriers. Theoretical and practical implications were discussed.

records.title: I Did It My Way Theatre: Research and Live Theatre as Applied to the Transition of Relocating Older Adults
records.abstract: Relocation is an option for older adults who leave their home to improve their emotional well-being, physical health, and safety. Moves can enhance agency or foster a loss of empowerment. We explored older adults’ transition experiences from a community setting to a retirement community and created messaging to help with experiences of older adults and their self-identified family or friend caregivers. We conducted 30 telephone interviews and analyzed relocation experiences, which informed I Did It My Way Theatre. The theatrical presentation was performed for over 100 older adult residents and caregivers. Our goal was to ease the transition experiences by disseminating findings to those involved in similar relocation situations. Attendees completed a post-performance questionnaire asking how the play helped them understand relocation and held table discussions concerning production themes. Follow-up interviews with 11 participants revealed that the play delivered hard messages in an impactful way.

records.title: Dementia Knowledge Among Older Asian Americans: Roles of Digital Literacy, Planning Attitudes, and Sociocultural Contexts
records.abstract: Knowledge of dementia facilitates early detection, care planning, and stigma reduction, yet less is known about dementia knowledge among Asian American populations. This study examined correlates of dementia knowledge among 505 Chinese, Korean, and Vietnamese Americans aged 50 and older residing in Central Florida. Dementia knowledge was assessed using the Dementia Knowledge Assessment Scale with four subscales. Linear regression analyses examined associations of dementia knowledge with sociodemographic, immigration, social, digital and information, and dementia experiences and attitudinal factors. Participants demonstrated low overall dementia knowledge. Digital literacy was positively associated with total dementia knowledge and all subscales except communication and behavior. Limited English proficiency was negatively associated with knowledge in the causes and characteristics subscale. The perceived importance of dementia planning was positively associated with total dementia knowledge and three subscales. Subscale-specific findings should be interpreted cautiously because of varying subscale reliability, particularly for communication and behavior.

Women aged ≥70 years, diagnosed between 2003-2009 with hormone receptor-positive (HR+), human epidermal growth factor 2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer were included, excluding those treated with chemotherapy or neoadjuvant therapy.
